name: Database vs File System
description: Comparison between file-based data storage and DBMS, focusing on redundancy, data anomaly, isolation, and concurrent access control.

name: DBMS Architecture
description: Three-schema architecture (Internal, Conceptual, External) and physical/logical data independence.

name: Data Models
description: High-level data abstractions including Relational, Object-Oriented, Network, and Hierarchical data models.

name: Entity
description: Definition of real-world objects (entities), entity sets, and strong vs weak entity sets.

name: Attribute
description: Types of attributes in ER modeling: simple, composite, single-valued, multivalued, and derived attributes.

name: Relationship
description: Associations between entities, degree of relationship sets (binary, ternary), and descriptive attributes.

name: Cardinality
description: Mapping cardinalities (1:1, 1:N, N:1, M:N) and participation constraints (total vs partial).

name: ER Diagram
description: Graphical representation of ER enterprise schemas and algorithmic reduction of ER diagrams to relational tables.

name: Relation
description: Mathematical relation concept, relational database schemas, instances, and structural constraints.

name: Tuple
description: Definition of rows/records (tuples), attribute domains, atomic values, and tuple unorderliness.

name: Relational Attribute
description: Named columns in a relation schema, domain constraints, and null values.

name: Super Key
description: Set of one or more attributes that collectively uniquely identify a tuple within a relation.

name: Candidate Key
description: Minimal super key with no redundant attributes capable of uniquely identifying tuples.

name: Primary Key
description: Candidate key chosen by the database designer as the principal means of identifying tuples.

name: Foreign Key
description: Attribute in a relation referencing a primary key in another relation, establishing referential integrity.

name: Functional Dependency
description: Constraint X -> Y between two sets of attributes in a relation, formal definition and semantics.

name: Trivial Dependency
description: Functional dependency X -> Y where Y is a subset of X, vs non-trivial and completely non-trivial FDs.

name: Closure
description: Closure F+ of a set of functional dependencies and Armstrong's Axioms (Reflexivity, Augmentation, Transitivity).

name: Attribute Closure
description: Algorithm to compute the set X+ of all attributes functionally determined by attribute set X under F.

name: 1NF
description: First Normal Form requiring attribute values to be atomic and eliminating repeating groups.

name: 2NF
description: Second Normal Form requiring 1NF and elimination of partial dependencies of non-prime attributes on candidate keys.

name: 3NF
description: Third Normal Form requiring 2NF and elimination of transitive dependencies of non-prime attributes on candidate keys.

name: BCNF
description: Boyce-Codd Normal Form requiring that for every non-trivial FD X -> Y, X must be a super key.

name: Transaction Concept
description: Logical unit of work executing single or multiple SQL statements, transaction states (Active, Partially Committed, Committed, Failed, Aborted).

name: ACID
description: Atomicity, Consistency, Isolation, and Durability principles governing transaction execution.

name: Serializability
description: Theoretical criterion for correctness of concurrent execution schedules.

name: Conflict Serializability
description: Conflict equivalent serial schedules and testing using serialization precedence graphs.

name: Concurrency Control
description: Locking protocols (2PL, Strict 2PL), Shared/Exclusive locks, and Timestamp Ordering protocols.

name: SELECT
description: Formulating projection and selection queries using SELECT statements and expressions.

name: WHERE
description: Row filtering conditions using logical operators, range tests, and pattern matching.

name: GROUP BY
description: Grouping rows sharing values into summary rows.

name: HAVING
description: Filtering aggregated group results produced by GROUP BY clauses.

name: JOIN
description: Combining rows from two or more tables (INNER, LEFT, RIGHT, FULL OUTER, CROSS JOIN).

name: Subquery
description: Nested queries, scalar subqueries, IN/EXISTS predicates, and correlated subqueries.

name: Aggregate Functions
description: Functions operating on collections of values (SUM, AVG, COUNT, MIN, MAX).

name: Index Concept
description: Auxiliary data structures to speed up record retrieval, ordered indices vs hash indices, clustered vs unclustered.

name: B-Tree
description: Balanced search trees (B-Tree and B+ Tree) structures, node fanout, height, and search/insert complexity.

name: Hash Index
description: Static and dynamic hashing techniques (Extendible & Linear Hashing) for equality lookups.

name: Index Trade-offs
description: Performance impact of indexing on SELECT queries versus INSERT, UPDATE, and DELETE operations.
